main.Figure_1_tract_maps.png: Figure 1. Mapped cafe density and modeled frequent mental distress in the three most populous study counties. Panels A–B show Los Angeles, C–D Cook and E–F Harris. Each measure uses pooled study-wide color limits: zero to the 99th percentile for cafe density and the 1st to 99th percentiles for mental distress. White areas are outside included tract polygons. Albers equal-area projection; scale bars differ between counties. Analytical assignment used full TIGER/Line geometry. Sources: © OpenStreetMap contributors, snapshot 31 December 2022; CDC PLACES 2024; ACS 2018–2022; US Census Bureau. Map lines delineate study areas and do not necessarily depict accepted national boundaries.
main.Figure_2_primary_adjustment.png: Figure 2. Primary cafe coefficient across progressively adjusted models. Points show percentage-point differences in modeled frequent mental distress per one-unit increase in log2(1 + cafes per 10,000 residents); bars are 95% county-cluster confidence intervals. All models use the same 23,527 tracts in 50 counties. The extended model adds poverty, unemployment, education, age composition, racial/ethnic composition and vehicle access to county and population-density adjustment; the final model also adds noncafe hospitality density. The extended-model absolute coefficient is 76.5% smaller than the unadjusted coefficient. This change is descriptive and is not a mediated or causal fraction. Intervals condition on PLACES point estimates and omit their unknown joint estimation uncertainty.
main.Figure_3_outcome_associations.png: Figure 3. Associations between mapped cafe availability and eight modeled health outcomes. Points and 95% county-cluster intervals compare unadjusted and extended models. The common exposure is log2(1 + cafes per 10,000 residents). Extended models include county fixed effects and eight prespecified contextual covariates. Intervals condition on the supplied PLACES point estimates; they do not include unknown joint source estimation uncertainty. Secondary-outcome BH and BY results are reported in the analytical tables.
main.Figure_4_contextual_correlates.png: Figure 4. Primary-model associations per observed standard deviation of each continuous predictor. Points and 95% county-cluster intervals concern modeled frequent mental distress. The fitted model uses natural units; standardization is for display. Several covariates overlap information used to generate PLACES estimates. Their relative magnitudes do not rank causal importance, and racial/ethnic composition describes structural context rather than biological effects.
main.Figure_5_association_shape.png: Figure 5. Exploratory quadratic exposure model for frequent mental distress. The contrast compares each density with zero mapped cafes while holding county and contextual covariates constant. Shading is the conditional 95% county-cluster interval. The curve stops at the observed 99th exposure percentile. The quadratic term on the transformed exposure scale had p = 0.901; curvature on the raw-density axis also reflects the log transformation. This plot does not estimate the effect of opening a cafe.

supplement.Figure_S1_study_counties.png: Figure S1. Population-selected county sampling frame. Teal areas are the 50 counties and county equivalents chosen using summed ACS 2018–2022 resident populations in SVI 2022. Gray states provide geographical context within the bounding box of the selected counties. Census cartographic boundaries are displayed in the contiguous-US Albers projection. This sample does not represent all US or global neighborhoods. Map lines delineate study areas and do not necessarily depict accepted national boundaries.
supplement.Figure_S2_exposure_distribution.png: Figure S2. Distribution of mapped cafe counts and transformed cafe density across 23,527 included tracts. The left panel groups counts of 20 or more in the terminal bar; the right shows log2(1 + cafes per 10,000 residents). Zero counts are retained. They indicate no qualifying mapped feature and do not establish complete business absence.
